standard_prerequisites.name: Induction principle of 0-truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For B : trunc0 A -> type with g : prd a:A B(|a|_0), assuming each B(x) is a set, there is f : prd x:trunc0 A B(x) with f(|a|_0) := g(a).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied twice: once in the constant-family form at source line 1126 to build the map from right to left, and once at source line 1127 to build h'.

standard_prerequisites.name: The 0-truncation is a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: trunc0 A is a set, so its path types are mere propositions.
standard_prerequisites.use: Together with B being a set it makes the goal h(x) = h'(x) at source line 1130 a mere proposition.

core_obligations: Apply the induction principle of 0-truncation to the constant family to obtain a map (A -> B) -> (trunc0 A -> B) and observe that it is a right inverse of composition with |.|_0 (source line 1126).
To see that it is also a left inverse, fix h : trunc0 A -> B and define h' : trunc0 A -> B by applying the induction principle to the composite a |-> h(|a|_0) (source line 1127).
Record the pointwise equality h'(|a|_0) = h(|a|_0) for all a : A that this definition gives (source line 1128).

Use that B is a set to see that h(x) = h'(x) is a mere proposition for every x : trunc0 A, and then apply the induction principle a second time to convert the pointwise statement into h(x) = h'(x) for all x, hence h = h' (source lines 1130-1131).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the map from right to left by the constant-family case of the induction principle and check the right-inverse computation.
Build h' by a second application of the induction principle and record its pointwise agreement with h.
Recognise the goal as a mere proposition and promote the pointwise equality to all of trunc0 A.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.9.2 at source lines 1120-1124: for every set B and every type A, composition with |.|_0 : A -> trunc0 A is an equivalence from trunc0 A -> B to A -> B. The proof is not a single appeal to the induction principle: the constant-family case at source line 1126 gives the map from right to left and only the right-inverse computation, and the left-inverse computation needs a second, differently instantiated application of the same induction principle at line 1127 together with the observation at line 1130 that h(x) = h'(x) is a mere proposition because B is a set. Only after that can the pointwise equality of line 1128 be promoted to all x : trunc0 A at line 1131.
